<PubmedArticle><MedlineCitation Status="MEDLINE" Owner="NLM" IndexingMethod="Curated"><PMID Version="1">42551713</PMID><DateCompleted><Year>2026</Year><Month>09</Month><Day>10</Day></DateCompleted><DateRevised><Year>2026</Year><Month>09</Month><Day>16</Day></DateRevised><Article PubModel="Print-Electronic"><Journal><ISSN IssnType="Electronic">1532-3064</ISSN><JournalIssue CitedMedium="Internet"><Volume>262</Volume><PubDate><Year>2026</Year><Month>Oct</Month></PubDate></JournalIssue><Title>Respiratory medicine</Title><ISOAbbreviation>Respir Med</ISOAbbreviation></Journal><ArticleTitle>Lung function after randomization to metformin, lifestyle intervention or placebo in the Diabetes Prevention Program Outcomes Study (DPPOS).</ArticleTitle><Pagination><StartPage>109077</StartPage><MedlinePgn>109077</MedlinePgn></Pagination><ELocationID EIdType="doi" ValidYN="Y">10.1016/j.rmed.2026.109077</ELocationID><ELocationID EIdType="pii" ValidYN="Y">S0954-6111(26)00445-2</ELocationID><Abstract><AbstractText Label="INTRODUCTION" NlmCategory="BACKGROUND">Metformin and physical activity have been suggested as beneficial for chronic lung disease; however, there are no prior randomized trials.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="METHODS" NlmCategory="METHODS">The Diabetes Prevention Program (DPP) was a 3-year trial that randomized 3234 individuals at risk for diabetes to metformin, lifestyle intervention or placebo. After the DPP, 88% of participants enrolled in the DPP Outcomes Study that offered lifestyle intervention to all and open-label continuation of metformin. Spirometry was performed at approximately 19 and 22 years post-randomization. Lung function measures were compared in an intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis by original randomization group. Models were unadjusted and adjusted for demographics, body size, smoking and sitting/standing at spirometry. Additional analyses tested prevalence of obstruction (FEV<sub>1</sub>/FVC <70%), restrictive pattern (FVC < LLN and FEV<sub>1</sub>/FVC ≥70%), preserved ratio impaired spirometry (PRISm: FEV<sub>1</sub> <80% predicted, FEV<sub>1</sub>/FVC ≥70%) and symptoms (COPD Assessment Test [CAT] score ≥10).</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="RESULTS" NlmCategory="RESULTS">The 1888 participants with spirometry were a mean (±SD) age of 68.2 ± 9.3 years, 70% female and 6% currently smoked and 33% had previously smoked cigarettes. Mean follow-up time was 19.0 ± 0.8 years. The mean FEV<sub>1</sub> was 2.14 ± 0.60 L, FVC 2.74 ± 0.74 L, FEV<sub>1</sub>/FVC 78.4 ± 6.4%, mean BMI was 32.4 ± 6.7 kg/m<sup>2</sup> and 58% had diabetes. In both unadjusted and adjusted ITT analyses, randomization group was not associated with FEV<sub>1</sub>, FVC or FEV<sub>1</sub>/FVC. Likewise, rates of obstruction, restrictive pattern, PRISm or symptoms did not differ by randomization group.</AbstractText><AbstractText Label="CONCLUSIONS" NlmCategory="CONCLUSIONS">In this long-term follow-up after a randomized trial, we found no significant associations between randomization to metformin or lifestyle intervention and lung function or respiratory symptoms.</AbstractText><CopyrightInformation>Copyright © 2026.
